subject: Processor-chain inventory request and escape-hatch plan
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@aurorahealth.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: security@aurorahealth.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Request: full processor-chain inventory + escape-hatch plan

Hi Markus,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our data processing review ahead of contract signature we need a single-file inventory of all downstream processors that may handle Aurora Health data (including temporary/transient vendors, telemetry processors, and any 3rd-party SaaS used by Redwood) with the following columns: vendor name, primary role, data types processed, country/jurisdiction of processing, encryption at rest/in transit (Y/N), KMS jurisdiction, access control model, and any available audit evidence (SOC2/ISO/attestation link).

Separately, could you also attach a concise "escape-hatch" plan describing: how Redwood would route EU-resident traffic on short notice (onshore fallback options), how to revoke a processor (data subject to deletion/retention steps), and the timeline/contacts for emergency cutover? We may need to present both documents to our procurement/security board next Friday (2026-12-18).

If you can get a draft by Monday (2026-12-14) that would help — we understand some vendors rotate frequently, so mark temporary entries clearly.

Appreciate it — we want to avoid last-minute surprises during the legal review.

Regards,
Lena Ortiz
Head of InfoSec, Aurora Health
security@aurorahealth.com

Attachment: (requested) inventory template schema
From: markus.klein@redwood.com <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: full processor-chain inventory + escape-hatch plan

Hi Lena —

Thanks for the clear ask. We'll produce two artifacts: (1) a single-sheet inventory CSV/XLSX that includes temporary processors flagged in a separate column, and (2) a one-page escape-hatch plan with runbooks and escalation contacts. We can provide SOC2/attestation links where available; if a vendor is not yet audited we'll note their current certification status and expected evidence timeline.

Plan for delivery: draft inventory + draft escape-hatch on 2026-12-16 EOD PT; final versions (with any SOC2 packages attached) by 2026-12-20. If you need the board-ready package earlier, let us know and we can prioritize.

Quick questions:
- Do you want telemetry/metrics processors included (they see only telemetry but may store derivatives)?
- For KMS jurisdiction, do you need key origin only or both key origin + KMS operator?

Looping in Rishi (privacy/ops) and Laura (legal) to coordinate evidence pulls and any contractual notes.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Product Security, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@aurorahealth.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, security@aurorahealth.com
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 08:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: full processor-chain inventory + escape-hatch plan

Markus —

Thanks. Please include telemetry/metrics processors; they need to be visible even if they only retain aggregated logs. For KMS, include both key origin country and the operator (e.g. "AWS KMS (us-east-1) / Redwood-managed" or "Customer KMS (DE) / customer-managed").

One more ask: our procurement will need a signed attestation that Redwood will notify Aurora within 48 hours of any subprocessor addition that can materially affect data residency or access. Can you provide a DocuSign-ready attestation or confirm the exact contractual clause Redwood proposes? That will speed our internal approval.

If you can attach the draft inventory and a short escape-hatch PDF, we'll expedite review.

-Lena

On a related note, can you flag any vendors that currently fall within EU export control restrictions? We will redact anything we can't share publicly, but need to know if there are blockers for the board packet.
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@aurorahealth.com>, markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Processor-chain inventory request and escape-hatch plan

Lena / Markus — forwarding final package. Per Markus' note, we've compiled the inventory and the escape-hatch plan and attached the requested evidence where available. Key highlights:

- Inventory includes 52 entries (including 9 temporary/ephemeral processors). Columns: vendor, role, data types, country, encryption-at-rest, encryption-in-transit, KMS_jurisdiction_and_operator, access_controls, audit_evidence_link, temporary_flag, effective_date.
- Escape-hatch plan covers onshore fallback routes (EU -> EU onshore pool), emergency revocation steps (48–72 hour initial containment + 30-day data purge window for affected vendor), and named contacts for cutover (Ops, Legal, Customer Success).
- Vendors with export-control flags are called out in the "notes" column; two providers have pending exportability reviews (see inventory rows 17 and 39).

Attachments included (stubs referenced here):
- subprocessor_inventory_v1.xlsx (master sheet)
- escape-hatch-plan-v1.pdf (1-page runbook + escalation list)
- soc2-scope-summary.zip (redacted SOC2 reports and scope index)
- docusign-attestation-prep.pdf (attestation language we propose)

Links:
- Audit/Jira ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-1987
- DocuSign prep: https://app.docusign.com/prepare/ABC123-attestation

Next steps: Laura will coordinate the DocuSign flow if the attestation language looks acceptable; Markus/Rishi will remain point for evidence clarifications. If Aurora wants us to exclude any temporary processors from the public board packet we can provide a redacted export for sharing.

Let us know if you want a short call to walk the board through the escape-hatch timeline (15–20 minutes).

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Privacy & Compliance Lead, Redwood Inference
